description: Edits and simulates synchronous sequential logic circuits.

methods.name: clockStep(): void
methods.description: Advances a clock cycle, updates memory elements and combinational outputs, and records the resulting timeline samples.

methods.name: evaluate(): void
methods.description: Recomputes combinational outputs without advancing the clock, records a timeline sample and emits tp-logic-evaluate.

methods.name: resetSequentialState(): void
methods.description: Restores memory elements to their initial Boolean states, clears the timeline, recomputes outputs and emits tp-sequential-reset.

methods.name: run(period = 700): void
methods.description: Starts repeated clock steps every period milliseconds, clamped to at least 100. Does nothing if already running; nonfinite periods use 700.

methods.name: stop(): void
methods.description: Stops automatic clock stepping while preserving the current circuit state and timeline.

methods.name: toggle(id: string, propagate = true): boolean
methods.description: Inverts input or output id and returns its new Boolean value. Optionally propagates input changes through combinational logic and records a timeline sample; unsupported nodes throw.

events.name: tp-logic-evaluate
events.description: Emitted after combinational outputs are recomputed without advancing the clock; graph contains the resulting snapshot.

events.name: tp-logic-toggle
events.description: Emitted after an input node is toggled; id identifies the input, value is its new Boolean level, and graph contains the resulting snapshot.
events.detail: { id: string; value: boolean; graph: TpGraphDocument }

events.name: tp-sequential-clock
events.description: Emitted after a clock cycle has updated memory and settled combinational outputs. values maps memory-element IDs to their new Boolean states.

events.name: tp-sequential-reset
events.description: Emitted after memory elements return to their initial states and the timeline is cleared; graph contains the reset snapshot.

dependencies.name: tp-graph-logical-circuit
dependencies.summary: Interactive combinational logic circuit editor and simulator.

userHelp.introduction: The custom `<tp-graph-sequential-circuit>` element implements the <tp-icon name="graph-sequential-circuit" library="components" size="1.25em"></tp-icon> Sequential logical circuit functionality: edits and simulates synchronous sequential logic circuits.
userHelp.interactions:
#### Mouse interactions

| Control or gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Reset sequential state | The lower toolbar provides **Reset sequential state**, **Stop clock**, **Run clock**, and **Clock step**. |
| Using the component | A clock step first evaluates the complete combinational network from the current state, samples every D input, applies all Q values simultaneously, and evaluates the combinational outputs again. |
| Using the component | This two-phase update makes the result independent of flip-flop ordering. |

#### Keyboard interactions

| Key or gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move between the available controls. |
| Focused controls | Use each control’s standard keyboard interaction.  |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>?</kbd> | Open User Help for the component under the pointer, or the focused component if none is hovered. Include <kbd>Shift</kbd> if needed to type <kbd>?</kbd>. |
